newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Intermarche studies European alliance - paper.
newsitem.headline: French Intermarche studies European alliance - paper.

text.p: Privately-owned supermarkets group Intermarche, ranked second in France in terms of sales, may need to form a European alliance to expand its activities outside France, business daily Les Echos said on Thursday.

"We have no choice," the newspaper quoted Intermarche secretary general Alain Rocher as saying. "From here on, five or six major national groups will generate identical benefits from suppliers. The difference will be made abroad."
Intermarche's foreign sales represent only 10 percent of the 135-136 billion francs generated in France in 1996. "We need to bring this percentage to 30 percent by the year 2005," he said.
No-one at Intermarche was available for comment.

French food retailers have stepped up their efforts to expand internationally as a result of a restrictive retail law passed in France last year that makes it harder for big stores to open new outlets or expand existing ones.
Intermarche, which operates the Mousquetaires chain, ranks sixth among European food retailers.

Although it recently sold eight stores in Spain and pulled out of Germany, Rocher said that did not signal that the group was turning inward. He said it had merely shed some of the outlets that were least profitable.

He said the group wants to strengthen its presence in Spain, where it has 35 stores, by adding 20 more. It wants to double the number of stores in Italy, currently eight, and increase its business in Belgium. Rocher said the group had sent teams to Britain and Ireland.
"And we're not inactive in eastern Europe," he said.

Rocher said the group did not have the means to expand alone and may need to forge an alliance with another independent group. "Barring that, we may find ourselves sidelined," he said. "We're in discussions," he added, but would not elaborate.
